items.text: Good morning, Tao. Thank you for meeting with me today.
Good morning, Tao. Thank you for meeting with me. Could you briefly introduce yourself and describe your current research?
Could you give me a short overview of your C. elegans lactylome study, and explain its main objective?
How did you prepare the samples and identify the lactylated peptides by mass spectrometry?
What was the most important finding, and how did you assess the reliability of the lactylation sites?
Which mass spectrometers and acquisition strategies have you used most independently?
Please describe one technical problem you encountered in a proteomics experiment, and explain how you solved it.
Why are you interested in visiting my group at Oxford?
What research question would you like to address during a three-to-six-month visit?
How would your experience in lactylation, phosphoproteomics, or single-cell multi-omics contribute to our work?
How would your visit be funded, and are there any conditions attached to that funding?
When would you be available to start, and how long could you stay in Oxford?
Finally, what questions would you like to ask me about the project or the group?
Could you tell me more specifically how your current work relates to mass spectrometry-based proteomics?
What biological question were you trying to answer with the lactylome study?
Which step in the experimental workflow was the most technically demanding for you?
How did you distinguish a reliable lactylation site from a possible false positive?
Could you name the instrument and software that you can operate most confidently?
Which aspect of our work on ubiquitin or protease biology is most relevant to your research goals?
What specific result would you hope to achieve by the end of a short visit?
Would the funding cover your travel, accommodation, and living costs in Oxford?
How flexible would you be if the laboratory needed to adjust the starting date?
My research focuses on mass spectrometry-based proteomics, particularly protein lactylation and phosphoproteomics.
The main objective of our study was to characterise the lactylome of C. elegans and explore its potential biological significance.
We prepared the samples carefully and used mass spectrometry-based analysis to identify lactylated peptides and modification sites.
Our most important finding was that lactylation may be associated with specific biological processes in C. elegans.
I have hands-on experience in proteomic sample preparation, mass spectrometry data acquisition, and downstream data analysis.
I am particularly interested in your group's expertise in ubiquitin biology, proteases, and mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
During the visit, I hope to develop a focused and feasible project that complements the group's current priorities.
I plan to apply for funding from the China Scholarship Council, subject to the relevant approval requirements.
I am flexible about the starting date and would be available for a research visit of three to six months.
Could you please advise me which research direction would be most useful for your group at present?
